category: AC/DC Rotating Machinery, Multiphysics Couplings, Studies and Results; MEMS Module Couplings
description: Rotating-machine features of Rotating Machinery, Magnetic (rmm) and Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic (mmtp), AC/DC multiphysics couplings and predefined interfaces, AC/DC-specific study steps and postprocessing variables, plus the MEMS Module piezoresistivity, pyroelectricity, thermoelasticity and thin-film damping functionality documented in the COMSOL 6.4 AC/DC and MEMS Module User's Guides. Java type strings were verified against the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Magnetic field, energy and matrix variables (mf.normB, mf.Qh, mf.intWm, mfco.Lac)
tools.description: Frequently used result variables of the magnetic interfaces (prefix = interface tag): mf.normB, mf.Bx/By/Bz, mf.normH, mf.Az (2D), current density mf.Jx/Jy/Jz and mf.normJ, total loss density mf.Qh and resistive loss mf.Qrh, total magnetic energy mf.intWm, inductance-matrix entries such as mf.L_1_2 from port/terminal sweeps, surface-current mfnc.normtB for shields, and matrix variables of Magnetic Fields, Currents Only (mfco.Ldc, mfco.Lac, mfco.Rdc, mfco.Rac, mfco.Z). In Rotating Machinery, Magnetic, rmm.Tark_1 and rmm.freqTP; in the time-periodic interface mmtp.phaseTP and frame values like mmtp.AZ_tp0.
tools.usage: Results > plot/evaluation Expression fields, e.g. Surface: mf.normB; Volume Integration: mf.Qh; Global Evaluation: mf.intWm, mfco.Lac; Global Matrix Evaluation: mfco.Ldc

parameters.name: normB / normH / normJ
parameters.description: Field magnitudes (T, A/m, A/m^2).

parameters.name: Qh / Qrh
parameters.description: Total and resistive volumetric loss density (W/m^3; cycle-averaged in frequency domain).

parameters.name: intWm
parameters.description: Total magnetic energy (J), useful for energy-based inductance L = 2*Wm/I^2.

parameters.name: Ldc, Lac, Rdc, Rac
parameters.description: mfco lumped inductance/resistance matrices from source sweeps.

tools.notes: Names confirmed from expressions in the 6.4 AC/DC Application Library (e.g. inductor_3d, ecore_transformer, helmholtz_coil, inductance_matrix_pcb_coils). Use the Replace Expression list in any plot to browse all variables of an interface.

tools.name: Electric field, terminal and lumped-matrix variables (es.normE, es.C11, es.Cinv11, ec.R11, es.Y11)
tools.description: Common result variables of Electrostatics (es), Electric Currents (ec) and Electric Currents in Shells (ecis): es.normE and components es.Ex/Ey/Ez, terminal quantities es.V0_1, es.Q0_1, es.I0_1 and ec.I0_1, ec.V0_1, lumped matrices es.C11 (Maxwell capacitance), es.Cinv11 (inverse Maxwell capacitance from Stationary Source Sweep), ec.R11 (resistance), admittance es.Y11/ec.Y11 and S-parameters es.S22dB from terminal sweeps, ec.normJ, ec.Qrh (Joule heat), ecis.Vav and ecis.Qsh on shells, and the excited-terminal potential es.VexcTerm during source sweeps.
tools.usage: Global Evaluation / Global Matrix Evaluation: es.C11, es.Cinv, ec.R11, es.Y11; Surface plots: es.normE, ec.normJ, ec.Qrh

parameters.name: V0_<n>, Q0_<n>, I0_<n>
parameters.description: Voltage, charge and current of terminal <n>.

parameters.name: Cij, Cinvij, Rij, Yij, Sij
parameters.description: Matrix elements indexed by terminal names.

parameters.name: Qrh
parameters.description: Resistive heating density (W/m^3).

tools.notes: Names confirmed from expressions in 6.4 library models (capacitive_position_sensor, capacitor_dc, busbar_terminal, piezoelectric devices). Matrix variables only exist after terminal sweeps or source-sweep studies.

tools.name: Accurate Coil Voltage Calculation (3D homogenized multiturn coils)
tools.description: Coil option (Stabilization section, on by default in Time Dependent and Frequency Domain studies) for 3D Homogenized multiturn coils that filters the applied external current density to make it numerically divergence free, by solving for an extra scalar filtering variable V_f in the coil domain. This removes spurious electric fields and greatly improves the lumped coil voltage and the impedance, inductance and power derived from it; inlet/outlet boundaries come from the geometry analysis, the Input/Output subnodes, or an Override Coil Inlet/Outlet subnode.
tools.usage: Coil > Show More Options > Stabilization > Accurate coil voltage calculation (checkbox); right-click Coil > Override Coil Inlet/Outlet when automatic detection fails

parameters.name: Accurate coil voltage calculation
parameters.description: Enable/disable the divergence filtering (default on in time/frequency studies).

parameters.name: Override Coil Inlet/Outlet
parameters.description: Manual inlet/outlet boundaries for Linear/Circular coils.

parameters.name: Input/Output (User Defined Coil Geometry)
parameters.description: Needed for user-defined direction fields.

tools.example: Toroidal multiturn coil in Frequency Domain: solve once with Accurate coil voltage calculation on and once off, and compare mf.VCoil_1 and mf.LCoil_1 against a mesh refinement to see the reduced mesh sensitivity.
tools.notes: Only available for the Homogenized multiturn conductor model.

tools.name: Frequency-domain loss models (complex permittivity, loss tangent, complex permeability)
tools.description: AC/DC guidance for losses in time-harmonic studies: dielectric losses are modelled with a complex permittivity epsilon' - i*epsilon'' (optionally separating conduction losses) or a loss tangent (loss angle or dissipation factor), in which case conductivity is set to zero; magnetic losses use the complex relative permeability mu' - i*mu'' (Magnetic losses magnetization model). Depending on COMSOL's time-harmonic sign convention, literature data may have to be conjugated; the loss density appears in <tag>.Qh for Electromagnetic Heating.
tools.usage: Charge Conservation / Current Conservation > Constitutive Relation D-E: Dielectric losses | Loss tangent; Ampère's Law > Magnetization model: Magnetic losses

parameters.name: epsilonPrim / epsilonBis
parameters.description: Real and imaginary relative permittivity.

parameters.name: tanDelta / delta
parameters.description: Dissipation factor or loss angle.

parameters.name: murPrim / murBis
parameters.description: Real and imaginary relative permeability.

tools.example: Cable insulation at 50 Hz: Current Conservation with Loss tangent, dissipation factor tan(delta) = 5e-4 and epsilon' = 2.3; integrate ec.Qh over the insulation for dielectric loss per metre.
tools.notes: Use Dispersion subnodes for frequency-dependent relaxation behaviour and Loss Calculation + Time-to-Frequency Losses for nonlinear time-domain iron loss.

tools.name: Mixed Formulation Boundary (Rotating Machinery, Magnetic)
tools.description: Default boundary feature of Rotating Machinery, Magnetic that imposes continuity between the magnetic scalar potential Vm on one side and the magnetic vector potential A on the other, so current-free regions (air, laminated iron) can use the cheaper Vm formulation while conductors and coils use A. It is applied automatically to all appropriate boundaries between Magnetic Flux Conservation and Ampère's Law domains.
tools.usage: Rotating Machinery, Magnetic > Mixed Formulation Boundary (default, automatic selection). Java: physics("rmm").feature("mxb1") (type MixedFormulationBoundary)

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Automatic: all boundaries between A and Vm regions.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/generator_2d: iron and air in Vm (Magnetic Flux Conservation) and rotor magnets/coils in A (Ampère's Law), joined by the default Mixed Formulation Boundary.
tools.notes: Avoid scalar-potential regions that encircle vector-potential regions with nonclosed currents (see the COMSOL blog on 3D rotating machinery); Exterior Electric Insulation helps satisfy the topology rules.

tools.name: Arkkio Torque Calculation (Rotating Machinery, Magnetic)
tools.description: Domain feature applied to the air gap that computes the electromagnetic torque of a radial-flux machine by Arkkio's method, a volume-integral variant of the Maxwell stress tensor (T = n_sec * integral of r*Br*Bphi/mu0 over the gap volume / gap width), which is much less mesh dependent than the surface-integral Force Calculation. The torque is the global variable <tag>.Tark_<torque name>; azimuthal/radial force densities and flux densities are also provided.
tools.usage: Rotating Machinery, Magnetic > Domains > Arkkio Torque Calculation (with Continuity, Sector Symmetry or Arkkio Extra Circular Boundaries). Java: physics("rmm").create("ark1", "ArkkioTorqueCalculation", 2); set("TorqueName", "rotor")

parameters.name: TorqueName
parameters.description: Suffix of rmm.Tark_<name>.

parameters.name: ArkkioParameters
parameters.description: automatic (inner/outer radius rin/rout detected) or user defined.

parameters.name: SectorInputType / nsectors
parameters.description: Number of sectors (automatic from Sector Symmetry).

parameters.name: TorqueAxis / TorqueRotationPoint
parameters.description: Rotation axis and center.

parameters.name: DimensionTolerance
parameters.description: Tolerance for automatic entity identification (default 1e-4, advanced).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/pm_motor_2d_introduction: Arkkio Torque Calculation on the air-gap domains, torque ripple from rmm.Tark_1 versus rotor angle.
tools.notes: Only valid for cylindrical air gaps (radial flux machines).

tools.name: Arkkio Extra Circular Boundaries (Rotating Machinery, Magnetic)
tools.description: Boundary feature that supplies additional circular air-gap boundaries to the Arkkio Torque Calculation when they are not already defined by Continuity or Sector Symmetry pairs, e.g. when a motor is modelled without an assembly (union geometry). The Applicable Pair Region setting chooses Fallback and nonpair regions, Nonpair region or All regions.
tools.usage: Rotating Machinery, Magnetic > Boundaries > Arkkio Extra Circular Boundaries

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: Circular boundaries bounding the Arkkio integration region.

parameters.name: Allowed region
parameters.description: Fallback and nonpair regions, Nonpair region, All regions.

tools.example: Static torque of a PM motor built as a union: select the two air-gap circles in Arkkio Extra Circular Boundaries and compute rmm.Tark_1 in a parametric sweep of rotor angle.
tools.notes: Java type string not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Multiphase Winding with Phase subnodes (Rotating Machinery / Time Periodic)
tools.description: Winding feature for electric machines in Rotating Machinery, Magnetic and Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic that excites a set of coils with phase offsets: Excitation type Phase currents (peak current and initial electrical angle) or DQ currents (d/q components via Park and Clarke transforms with a synchronous reference frame). An automatic layout generates Phase subnodes (phase offset angles, e.g. 0, -120, -240 deg) from pole/slot counts, and homogenized multiturn wire properties are set as for Coil. A Loss Calculation subnode can be added in rmm; mmtp computes losses internally.
tools.usage: Rotating Machinery, Magnetic > Multiphase Winding > Phase. Java: physics("rmm").create("wnd1", "MultiphaseWinding", 2); set("ExcitationType", "PhaseCurrents"); set("Ipk", "I0"); set("NoPoles", "8"); set("NoSlots", "48")

parameters.name: WindingName
parameters.description: Suffix for winding variables.

parameters.name: ExcitationType
parameters.description: PhaseCurrents (Ipk, alpha_i) or DQ currents (Id, Iq, alpha_d).

parameters.name: freq_t / ReferenceFrameDefinition
parameters.description: Electrical frequency and synchronous frame definition.

parameters.name: WindingLayout / NoPoles / NoSlots / NoCoilsPerSlot / CoilSpan
parameters.description: Automatic three-phase layout generation.

parameters.name: N, sigmaCoil, FillingFactor
parameters.description: Turns per coil and wire properties (homogenized multiturn).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/pm_motor_2d_introduction and interior_pm_motor_stress_analysis (three-phase winding, automatic Phase subnodes).
tools.notes: Phase subnode: phase offset angle for the selected slot domains (signal function cos by default).

tools.name: Conducting Magnet / Nonconducting Magnet (Rotating Machinery, Magnetic)
tools.description: The Magnet feature as it appears in Rotating Machinery, Magnetic: Conducting Magnet (vector-potential formulation, eddy currents allowed, optional insulation per segment and Loss Calculation) and Nonconducting Magnet (scalar-potential region, no induced currents). Both define magnetization direction from North/South boundaries, domains or a vector with Circular/Linear patterns, typically Alternating for rotor poles.
tools.usage: Rotating Machinery, Magnetic > Conducting Magnet / Nonconducting Magnet. Java: physics("rmm").create("cmag1", "ConductingMagnet", 2); set("PatternType", "CircularPattern"); ("ncmag1", "NonconductingMagnet", 3)

parameters.name: DirectionMethod / PatternType / PeriodicType
parameters.description: As for Magnet (North/South, circular pattern, alternating).

parameters.name: ConstitutiveRelationBH
parameters.description: RemanentFluxDensity by default.

parameters.name: ConstrainForInducedCurrents
parameters.description: Insulate each magnet domain (segmented magnets).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/generator_2d (Conducting Magnet with circular alternating pattern); rotating_machinery_3d_tutorial uses Nonconducting Magnet.
tools.notes: Choose Conducting Magnet when magnet eddy-current loss matters (high-speed machines).

tools.name: Rotating Domain (Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic)
tools.description: Domain feature of the time-periodic machinery interface that declares which domains rotate and links the mechanical rotation to the time-periodic phase: the rotation angle during one time-periodic cycle alpha_TP is Synchronous (pole pair) 4*pi/n_poles, Full mechanical revolution (+/-2*pi by direction), Nonrotating or User defined (default expression if(mmtp.NoPoles==0,2*pi,4*pi/mmtp.NoPoles)). User-defined angles model slip in asynchronous machines. Works with Rotational Magnetic Continuity; each Rotating Domain should cover exactly one geometry component.
tools.usage: Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic > Rotating Domain. Java: physics("mmtp").create("tprot1", "TimePeriodicRotatingDomain", 2); set("TimePeriodicRotationType", "SyncrhonousPolePair")

parameters.name: TimePeriodicRotationType
parameters.description: Synchronous (pole pair), FullMechanicalRevolution, Nonrotating, User defined.

parameters.name: RotationDirection
parameters.description: Counterclockwise or Clockwise.

parameters.name: RotationAngleDuringTimePeriodicCycle
parameters.description: alpha_TP expression (user defined).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/pmm_steady_state: rotor as Rotating Domain with synchronous rotation over one electrical period.
tools.notes: Rotation features require Motion type = Rotational motion in the interface settings; the Add Rotational Boundary Features button sets up typical pairs.

tools.name: Rotational Magnetic Continuity / Rotational Periodicity (Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic)
tools.description: Rotational Magnetic Continuity is a pair condition applying phase-dependent continuity of the vector potential across the sliding rotor–stator interface of parts rotating at different speeds; it also defines the phase-dependent axial torque <tag>.<feature>.Tax_tpph via an Arkkio-like procedure. Rotational Periodicity imposes periodicity or antiperiodicity between the radial boundaries when only one sector of the machine is modelled; both work together with Rotating Domain.
tools.usage: Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic > Pairs > Rotational Magnetic Continuity; Boundaries > Rotational Periodicity. Java: physics("mmtp").create("drcon1", "RotationalContinuityPair", 1); create("drper1", "RotationalPeriodicity", 1)

parameters.name: SelectionType / RotationNSectors
parameters.description: FullCircle or Sector and number of sectors.

parameters.name: RotationalPeriodicityType
parameters.description: Continuity, Antiperiodicity or From physics periodicity.

parameters.name: pairs
parameters.description: Identity pair on the sliding boundary.

parameters.name: TransformationMethod
parameters.description: Automatic source/destination mapping for Rotational Periodicity.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/pm_motor_2d_efficiency_map: one pole-pair sector with Rotational Periodicity and a Rotational Magnetic Continuity pair; torque mmtp.drcon1.Tax_tpph plotted over the phase.
tools.notes: See 'Typical Setup of Rotating Domain, Rotational Magnetic Continuity, and Rotational Periodicity' in the AC/DC User's Guide.

tools.name: Time-periodic phase variables _tpph / _tpN (mmtp results)
tools.description: Result variables of the Magnetic Machinery, Rotating, Time Periodic interface that depend on the phase within the period: the suffix _tpph evaluates a quantity at the phase given by the dataset's phase parameter (e.g. mmtp.normB_tpph), and _tpN gives the value at time frame N = 0 ... nTP-1 (e.g. mmtp.normB_tp4 at phase pi/2 when nTP = 16). Available for current density, E, B, H, Az, feature voltages and force densities, and lumped quantities such as coenergy and axial torque (mmtp.<pairTag>.Tax_tpph).
tools.usage: Results > expressions such as mmtp.normB_tpph, mmtp.normB_tp0, mmtp.drcon1.Tax_tpph (set the phase in the dataset or evaluation)

parameters.name: _tpph
parameters.description: Value at the current phase (dataset/solution phase input).

parameters.name: _tpN
parameters.description: Value at time frame N.

parameters.name: Averages / RMS / FFT
parameters.description: Time-periodic averages, RMS, standard deviation and Fourier coefficients are available in evaluation.

tools.example: Global Evaluation of mmtp.drcon1.Tax_tpph with a parametric phase sweep in the dataset to plot torque ripple over one electrical period.
tools.notes: Force Calculation variables carry an extra user suffix, e.g. mmtp.<...>_tpph_<forceName>.

tools.name: Magnetohydrodynamics (multiphysics interface and coupling)
tools.description: Predefined interface (Magnetic and Electric Fields + Laminar Flow + Magnetohydrodynamics coupling mhd1) for conducting fluids in magnetic fields; the coupling passes the Lorentz force J x B to the flow and the motional EMF v x B back to the electromagnetic interface. The coupling also supports Magnetic Fields, Magnetic Field Formulation and Rotating Machinery, Magnetic, in 2D, 2D axisymmetric and 3D with Stationary, Time Dependent, Frequency–Stationary and Frequency–Transient studies. Use it for liquid-metal pumps, electromagnetic stirring, Hartmann flows and fusion blankets.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > AC/DC > Electromagnetics and Fluids > Magnetohydrodynamics. Java: multiphysics().create("mhd1", "Magnetohydrodynamics", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Magnetic interface (mef by default) and Laminar Flow.

parameters.name: Fluid domain feature
parameters.description: Use Ampère's Law and Current Conservation in Fluids in the fluid.

parameters.name: Moving mesh
parameters.description: Add Deforming Domain/moving mesh when the conductor shape changes.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Fluids/hartmann_boundary_layer, magnetohydrodynamics_pump and hartmann_flow_in_liquid_metal_blanket.
tools.notes: Not for ferrofluids (magnetization forces need a user-defined coupling). Equilibrium plasma arcs use the Plasma/Electric Discharge equilibrium discharge interfaces instead.

tools.name: Magnetomechanics, Solid / Boundary (AC/DC–structure couplings)
tools.description: Couplings between magnetic fields and deforming structures: Magnetomechanics, Solid (mmcpl1) couples Magnetic Fields or Magnetic Fields, No Currents with Solid Mechanics (magnetic Maxwell stress on magnetic materials and Lorentz forces on conductors, with a moving mesh so deformation changes the field), and Magnetomechanics, Boundary (mmfb1) couples them to Shell or Membrane interfaces. Geometric nonlinearity is enforced (unless 'Only use Lorentz force' is selected for the solid coupling); frequency response uses prestressed or small-signal studies because the force is quadratic in the field.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > AC/DC > Electromagnetics and Mechanics > Magnetomechanics, Solid (or Shell/Membrane, and No Currents variants). Java: multiphysics().create("mmcpl1", "Magnetomechanics", 3); multiphysics().create("mmfb1", "MagnetomechanicsBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Solid Mechanics/Shell/Membrane and Magnetic Fields/Magnetic Fields, No Currents.

parameters.name: Only use Lorentz force
parameters.description: Neglect magnetization forces and geometric nonlinearity (solid coupling).

parameters.name: Studies
parameters.description: Stationary, Time Dependent, Eigenfrequency/Frequency Domain Prestressed, Small-Signal Analysis.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Mechanics/contactor_shading_coil and magnetic_damping (solid) and magnetic_diaphragm (boundary coupling with a Shell).
tools.notes: Requires AC/DC plus Structural Mechanics or MEMS Module. Nonlinear Magnetostriction and Piezomagnetism are separate couplings.

tools.name: Magnetic Forces, Rotating Machinery (mfrm coupling)
tools.description: The Magnetic–Elastic Interaction in Rotating Machinery interface (3D, planar 2D) combines Solid Mechanics with Rotating Machinery, Magnetic plus moving-mesh features and the Magnetic Forces, Rotating Machinery coupling (mfrm1), which transfers magnetic forces on magnets, laminations and solid iron to the rotating and stationary structures and lets deformation feed back into the field. It computes stresses in rotors (e.g. magnet retention in IPM rotors at speed) and stator vibration loads; a Magnetic–Rigid Body Interaction variant couples to Multibody Dynamics.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > AC/DC > Electromagnetics and Mechanics > Magnetic–Elastic Interaction in Rotating Machinery. Java: multiphysics().create("mfrm1", "MagneticForcesRotatingMachinery", 2)

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: Intersection of solid domains and applicable rmm features (Ampère's Law in solids, Magnet, laminated cores).

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Solid Mechanics (or Multibody Dynamics) and Rotating Machinery, Magnetic.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/interior_pm_motor_stress_analysis and pm_motor_2d_structure_interaction.
tools.notes: Geometric nonlinearity is enforced on applicable study steps. Requires AC/DC plus Structural Mechanics (or Multibody Dynamics) Module.

tools.name: Induction Heating (multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface combining Magnetic Fields and Heat Transfer in Solids with the Electromagnetic Heating coupling for induction and eddy-current heating, with temperature-dependent electromagnetic properties. Because the magnetic cycle is short compared with thermal time scales, it is normally solved with Frequency–Stationary or Frequency–Transient studies (frequency-domain EM + stationary/transient heat), including one-way variants and Small-Signal Analysis. Available in 3D, 2D and 2D axisymmetry.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > AC/DC > Electromagnetic Heating > Induction Heating (adds mf, ht and emh1). Java: multiphysics().create("emh1", "ElectromagneticHeating", 3)

parameters.name: Coil (mf)
parameters.description: Induction coil excitation (current, voltage, power in 2D).

parameters.name: Electromagnetic Heating coupling
parameters.description: Passes cycle-averaged losses mf.Qh to ht and T back to mf.

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Frequency–Transient (FrequencyTransient) or Frequency–Stationary (FrequencyStationary).

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Electromagnetic_Heating/inductive_heating, induction_heating_curie_movement and ACDC_Module/Applications/billet_induction_heating.
tools.notes: Low frequencies approaching the static limit make the frequency formulation ill posed; add small conductivity in air or use the stabilization settings. Joule Heating (ec + ht) is catalogued under 'Electromagnetic Heating / Joule Heating'.

tools.name: Symmetry Plane (Electrostatics / Magnetic Fields / Magnetic Fields, No Currents)
tools.description: Boundary condition in the AC/DC interfaces that represents a plane of symmetry or antisymmetry of the field so only part of a device needs to be modelled. For the electric field (Electrostatics) Symmetry sets n·E = 0 and Antisymmetry n x E = 0; for the magnetic flux density (Magnetic Fields) Symmetry sets n·B = 0 and Antisymmetry n x B = 0; for the magnetic field (Magnetic Fields, No Currents) Symmetry sets n·H = 0 and Antisymmetry n x H = 0.
tools.usage: Electrostatics / Magnetic Fields / Magnetic Fields, No Currents > Boundaries > Symmetry Plane. Java: physics("mfnc").create("symp1", "SymmetryPlane", 2); set symmetry type Symmetry or Antisymmetry

parameters.name: Symmetry type
parameters.description: Symmetry or Antisymmetry of the respective field.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries on the symmetry cut.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Introductory_Electrostatics/dielectric_shielding_comparison (es), ACDC_Module/Devices,_Resistive/magnetotellurics (mf) and ACDC_Module/Introductory_Magnetostatics/permanent_magnet (mfnc).
tools.notes: Magnetic Insulation (n x A = 0) is equivalent to a flux-parallel symmetry in mf; Perfect Magnetic Conductor to the opposite case. Remember to apply length/area correction factors to coil Geometry Analysis when cutting coils.

tools.name: Magnetic Continuity / Electric Continuity (AC/DC identity-pair conditions)
tools.description: Pair conditions that make fields continuous across identity (or contact) pairs of assembly geometries, e.g. the sliding rotor–stator interface of rotating machines or non-conformal meshed parts: Continuity in Magnetic Fields / Rotating Machinery, Magnetic ('Magnetic Continuity') and Electric Continuity in Electrostatics and Electric Currents. In 3D the magnetic version has Continuity Constraint Parameters Automatic (default; scalar potential on both sides with a mesh-dependent penalty, suited to motion and non-conformal meshes) or Legacy (equal vector potential, conformal meshes without motion only).
tools.usage: Magnetic Fields / Rotating Machinery, Magnetic > Pairs > Continuity; Electrostatics / Electric Currents > Pairs > Continuity. Java: physics("rmm").create("cont1", "Continuity", 1); set pairs

parameters.name: Pair selection
parameters.description: From list (default), All, All contact pairs, All identity pairs.

parameters.name: Continuity constraint parameters (3D mf)
parameters.description: Automatic or Legacy (requires conformal meshes).

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/generator_2d: identity pair on the air-gap circle created by Form Assembly, Continuity feature in Rotating Machinery, Magnetic, rotor on a Rotating Domain.
tools.notes: Use Sector Symmetry instead when only a sector is modelled; the Arkkio Torque Calculation can pick up Continuity boundaries automatically. Mesh the destination side finer for nonconforming pairs.

tools.name: Time-to-Frequency Losses (study step)
tools.description: Study step, normally placed after a Time Dependent step, that performs a forward FFT of the last electrical period [Te - T, Te] of the time-domain solution and evaluates the Loss Calculation subnodes (resistive heating, Steinmetz, Bertotti) by summing the harmonic contributions (6 harmonics by default). It gives accurate iron and copper losses of nonsinusoidal, saturated devices without the approximations of effective B-H curves.
tools.usage: Study > Study Steps > Frequency Domain > Time-to-Frequency Losses. Java: model.study("std1").create("emloss", "TimeToFrequencyLosses")

parameters.name: Input study
parameters.description: Study providing the time-domain data (or Current).

parameters.name: Number of harmonics
parameters.description: Harmonics included in the loss sum (default 6).

parameters.name: Electrical period
parameters.description: Taken from the Loss Calculation frequency settings (1/f).

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/ecore_transformer and ACDC_Module/Devices,_Motors_and_Generators/generator_2d: Time Dependent over several periods, then Time-to-Frequency Losses to get core loss density.
tools.notes: Loss Calculation subnodes must be present before the Time Dependent study is computed.

tools.name: Frequency–Stationary / Frequency–Transient (Induction Heating, MHD and ICP studies)
tools.description: Combined studies that solve electromagnetic fields in the frequency domain together with stationary (Frequency–Stationary) or time-dependent (Frequency–Transient) heat transfer, flow or other physics driven by cycle-averaged quantities (losses, time-averaged Lorentz force). Used by Induction Heating, Microwave/Laser Heating, Magnetohydrodynamics, Equilibrium Discharges and, with electron temperature, Inductively Coupled and Microwave Plasma. Other frequency-capable interfaces (e.g. Solid Mechanics) must set their equation form to Stationary/Transient.
tools.usage: Add Study > Preset Studies for Selected Multiphysics > Frequency–Transient / Frequency–Stationary. Java: model.study("std1").create("ftrans", "FrequencyTransient"); model.study("std1").create("fstat", "FrequencyStationary")

parameters.name: freq
parameters.description: Electromagnetic frequency.

parameters.name: Times (Frequency–Transient)
parameters.description: Output times for the transient part.

parameters.name: Physics and variables selection
parameters.description: Which interfaces are solved in the step.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Electromagnetic_Heating/induction_heating_curie_movement (Frequency–Transient) and ACDC_Module/Tutorials,_Cables/submarine_cable_06_thermal_effects (Frequency–Stationary).
tools.notes: Valid only when power transfer occurs at twice the EM frequency and thermal time scales are much longer than the period. For ICP, EEDF-dependent plasmas pair it with EEDF Initialization.

tools.name: Connecting Electrical Circuits to AC/DC Physics Interfaces (predefined and user-defined couplings)
tools.description: AC/DC modelling guide for field–circuit co-simulation: circuits connect through the External I vs. U, External U vs. I and External I-Terminal elements, and field features that support predefined couplings (Terminal and Floating Potential in electric interfaces, Coil and Lumped Port in magnetic interfaces, plus terminals/contacts in RF, MEMS, Plasma, Electric Discharge and Semiconductor interfaces) announce their voltage or current when set to Circuit type. For user-defined couplings, apply the circuit's current/voltage as an excitation and select a User-defined measurement; circuit state variables are named cir.Xn_v and cir.Xn_i (see Show Default Solver > Dependent Variables).
tools.usage: Set Terminal/Coil/Lumped Port excitation to Circuit, add Electrical Circuit > External I vs. U (or U vs. I / I-Terminal) and pick the announced voltage/current; or choose User defined and enter your own expression

parameters.name: Predefined coupling
parameters.description: Terminal type / Coil excitation 'Circuit' announces the variables.

parameters.name: User-defined coupling
parameters.description: Coupling operators and cir.Xn_v / cir.Xn_i state variables.

parameters.name: Ideal source rule
parameters.description: External elements are ideal sources: add a series/parallel resistor to avoid 'The DAE is structurally inconsistent'.

tools.example: Application Libraries ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Circuits/inductor_in_circuit (3D inductor in a transistor circuit) and ACDC_Module/Electromagnetics_and_Circuits/circuit_fem_resistor.
tools.notes: Solve field and circuit together (Fully Coupled); in Time Dependent studies avoid step changes in current-driven coils.

tools.name: Source Initialization (Magnetic Fields, Currents Only study step)
tools.description: Study step contained in the preset Stationary Source Sweep with Initialization and Frequency Domain Source Sweep with Initialization studies of Magnetic Fields, Currents Only; like Coil Geometry Analysis, it computes the current flow field in the Conductor/Multiterminal Conductor domains for each terminal before the source sweep assembles the inductance (and resistance) matrices.
tools.usage: Add Study > Stationary Source Sweep with Initialization (Source Initialization + Stationary Source Sweep). Java: model.study("std1").create("init", "SourceInitialization")

parameters.name: Follow-up step
parameters.description: Stationary Source Sweep or Frequency Domain Source Sweep.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Inductive/inductance_matrix_pcb_coils: Source Initialization then Frequency Domain Source Sweep to obtain the mfco inductance matrix of several PCB coils.
tools.notes: See also 'Stationary Source Sweep / Frequency Domain Source Sweep' and 'Global Matrix Evaluation'.

tools.name: Coil lumped variables (mf.VCoil_1, mf.ICoil_1, mf.RCoil_1, mf.LCoil_1, mf.ZCoil_1)
tools.description: Global variables defined by every coil feature with the template <scope>.<variable>Coil_<coil name>: VCoil (voltage), ICoil (current), PCoil (power), and derived lumped parameters. In Stationary and Time Dependent studies RCoil (resistance) is defined; in Frequency Domain studies ZCoil (impedance), RCoil (resistance), LCoil (inductance), XCoil (reactance) and YCoil (admittance); in Frequency-Domain Perturbation studies the impedance is computed from the harmonic perturbation voltage and current (lindev).
tools.usage: Results > Derived Values > Global Evaluation: mf.LCoil_1, real(mf.ZCoil_1), mf.PCoil_1 (replace mf with the interface tag and 1 with the coil name)

parameters.name: Coil name
parameters.description: Set in the Coil node (Coil Name field).

parameters.name: Study type
parameters.description: Determines which lumped variables exist.

parameters.name: Accurate coil voltage calculation
parameters.description: Coil setting improving VCoil in 3D time/frequency studies.

tools.notes: Circuit connections and Multiphase Windings define analogous winding variables. Inductance from energy (2*Wm/I^2) is an alternative check.

tools.name: Electromagnetic force, torque and loss variables (ForceX_<name>, Tax_<name>, FLtz, Qh)
tools.description: Postprocessing variables of the AC/DC interfaces: Force Calculation and Boundary Force Calculation define <tag>.Force<comp>_<name>, <tag>.Torque<comp>_<name> and axial torque <tag>.Tax_<name> (cycle-averaged versions in frequency domain); Lorentz force density <tag>.FLtz<comp> (J x B) exists in domains and on current-carrying boundaries; Arkkio torque <tag>.Tark_<name>; and the volumetric loss density <tag>.Qh (resistive + magnetic losses) that feeds Electromagnetic Heating.
tools.usage: Global Evaluation: mf.Forcez_rotor, mf.Tax_rotor, rmm.Tark_1; Volume Integration: mf.Qh; Arrow Volume: mf.FLtzx, mf.FLtzy, mf.FLtzz

parameters.name: <name>
parameters.description: Force/Torque name set in the calculation node.

parameters.name: <comp>
parameters.description: Spatial component x, y, z (r, phi, z in axisymmetry).

parameters.name: Maxwell stress vs. Lorentz
parameters.description: Force Calculation includes magnetization forces; FLtz only J x B.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Introductory_Electromagnetic_Forces/force_calculation_01_introduction introduces force evaluation with the Force Calculation feature; parallel_wires checks the Lorentz force between two conductors.
tools.notes: Surround the body with air (non-magnetic) for accurate Maxwell-stress forces; use Arkkio for machines.

tools.name: Lumped Parameter Conversion (Maxwell / mutual / SPICE capacitance, Z, Y, S matrices)
tools.description: AC/DC methods for lumped matrices: with forced voltage the terminal currents give the admittance matrix Y (capacitance in electrostatics); with fixed current the voltages give Z (energy method in magnetostatics); fixed charge gives the inverse capacitance matrix. Stationary Source Sweep produces the inverse Maxwell capacitance matrix (es, esbe) or the resistance matrix (ec), and Global Matrix Evaluation's Transformation section converts between Z, Y, S, Maxwell and mutual (SPICE) capacitance matrices; mutual capacitance diagonal = row sum of the Maxwell matrix, off-diagonals change sign.
tools.usage: Results > Derived Values > Global Matrix Evaluation > Transformation (Maxwell capacitance, Mutual capacitance, Z, Y, S); physics-level Manual Terminal Sweep / Port Sweep settings for Touchstone export

parameters.name: Terminal type
parameters.description: Voltage (Y/C matrix, recommended with reaction terms), Current (Z), Charge (C^-1).

parameters.name: Ground
parameters.description: At least one Ground is required for a proper matrix.

parameters.name: es.VexcTerm
parameters.description: Potential of the excited terminal during a Stationary Source Sweep.

parameters.name: Touchstone export
parameters.description: Z, Y or S matrices from terminal/port sweeps.

tools.example: Application Library ACDC_Module/Devices,_Capacitive/capacitive_position_sensor: Stationary Source Sweep over 5 terminals, Global Matrix Evaluation with Mutual capacitance transformation.
tools.notes: Declare either all voltage or all current terminals for a consistent matrix.

tools.name: AC/DC and Nonlinear Magnetic material libraries
tools.description: Material libraries used with the AC/DC Module: the AC/DC branch (conductors, magnets and soft materials, Liquid Metals for MHD, Biological Tissues with multipole Debye data for 54 tissues, and vendor data such as Bomatec NdFeB/SmCo/ferrite magnet grades) and the Nonlinear Magnetic branch with B-H curves for a large set of ferromagnetic alloys and steels. Example materials 'Nonlinear Permanent Magnet' (AlNiCo 5) and 'Jiles–Atherton Hysteretic Material' support the special magnetization models.
tools.usage: Home > Add Material > Material Library > AC/DC or Nonlinear Magnetic; or Materials > Add Material from Library

parameters.name: AC/DC > Hard Magnetic Materials
parameters.description: Remanent flux density norm and recoil permeability.

parameters.name: Nonlinear Magnetic
parameters.description: B-H curve and coenergy interpolation functions.

parameters.name: Liquid Metals / Biological Tissues
parameters.description: Conductivity, viscosity, density; Debye poles.

tools.example: Assign a sintered NdFeB magnet grade from the AC/DC branch to the rotor magnets and a Nonlinear Magnetic electrical steel (B-H curve) to the laminated core of a PM motor model.
tools.notes: Use ACDC_Module/Applications/bh_curve_checker to inspect and extrapolate custom B-H data.

tools.name: Piezoresistivity, Domain Currents (MEMS multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined multiphysics interface (Solid Mechanics + Electric Currents + Piezoresistivity, Domain Currents coupling pzrd1) for piezoresistors whose thickness is resolved by the mesh: the coupling computes the conductivity tensor from stress or strain in Linear Elastic (or Hyperelastic) Material and the coefficients in Current Conservation, Piezoresistive. Used for silicon pressure sensors, strain gauges and accelerometers with implanted resistors.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Piezoresistivity > Piezoresistivity, Domain Currents (adds solid, ec with Current Conservation, Piezoresistive, and the coupling)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Solid Mechanics and Electric Currents.

parameters.name: Domain selection
parameters.description: Domains with both Current Conservation, Piezoresistive and Linear Elastic Material.

parameters.name: Constitutive form
parameters.description: Piezoresistance (Pi_l) or elastoresistance (M_l) form in the Electric Currents node.

tools.example: Resolved n-type resistor on a diaphragm: Piezoresistivity, Domain Currents, Terminal 3 V / Ground at the resistor ends, Stationary pressure sweep, output ec.I0_1.
tools.notes: Up to COMSOL 5.2 this was a single physics interface; now it is a coupling. Java type string of the domain coupling not present in the 6.4 Application Library.

tools.name: Piezoresistivity, Boundary Currents (MEMS multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface (Solid Mechanics + Electric Currents in Shells + Piezoresistivity, Boundary Currents coupling pzrb1) for piezoresistive layers much thinner than the structural layer: the resistor is modelled on a boundary with the Piezoresistive Shell node while stress comes from the 3D solid. It avoids meshing thin implanted or deposited resistor layers.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Piezoresistivity > Piezoresistivity, Boundary Currents. Java: multiphysics().create("pzrb1", "PiezoresistiveEffectBoundary", 2)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Solid Mechanics and Electric Currents in Shells.

parameters.name: Piezoresistive Shell
parameters.description: Zero-stress conductivity and piezoresistance/elastoresistance matrix of the layer.

tools.example: Application Library MEMS_Module/Sensors/piezoresistive_pressure_sensor: Wheatstone-type x-ducer resistor on a silicon diaphragm; output voltage versus applied pressure.
tools.notes: Requires MEMS Module.

tools.name: Piezoresistivity, Shell / Layered Shell (MEMS multiphysics interfaces)
tools.description: Piezoresistivity, Shell combines the structural Shell interface with Electric Currents in Shells and the Piezoresistivity, Shell coupling (pzrs1) when the structure itself is thin enough for shell theory; Piezoresistivity, Layered Shell combines Layered Shell and Electric Currents in Layered Shells with the Piezoresistivity, Layered coupling (pzrl1), in piezoresistance or elastoresistance form. Both use the Piezoresistive Shell node for the electrical properties.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Piezoresistivity > Piezoresistivity, Shell / Piezoresistivity, Layered Shell. Java: multiphysics().create("pzrs1", "PiezoresistiveEffectShell", 2); multiphysics().create("pzrl1", "PiezoresistivityLS", 2)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Shell / Layered Shell and Electric Currents in (Layered) Shells.

parameters.name: Selection
parameters.description: Boundaries (and layers) where Piezoresistive Shell and Linear Elastic Material are both active.

tools.example: Application Libraries MEMS_Module/Sensors/piezoresistive_pressure_sensor_shell and Composite_Materials_Module/Multiphysics/piezoresistive_pressure_sensor_layered.
tools.notes: Shell variant needs the Structural Mechanics Module; Layered Shell variant needs the Composite Materials Module.

tools.name: Current Conservation, Piezoresistive (Electric Currents)
tools.description: Electric Currents domain node that holds the piezoresistive material data for the Piezoresistivity, Domain Currents coupling: Constitutive model Piezoresistance form (zero-stress conductivity and piezoresistance coupling matrix Pi_l, ohm·m/Pa) or Elastoresistance form (elastoresistance matrix M_l, ohm·m). Without an active coupling it behaves like Current Conservation with the zero-stress conductivity.
tools.usage: Electric Currents > Current Conservation, Piezoresistive (added automatically by Piezoresistivity, Domain Currents)

parameters.name: Constitutive model
parameters.description: Piezoresistance form or Elastoresistance form.

parameters.name: sigma0
parameters.description: Electric conductivity at zero stress (From material).

parameters.name: Pi_l / M_l
parameters.description: Piezoresistance or elastoresistance coupling matrix (Piezoresistivity material library).

tools.example: Assign a p-type silicon material from the Piezoresistivity material library to the resistor domains and use a rotated coordinate system aligned with the <110> crystal direction.
tools.notes: Material orientation matters: define a Rotated System for crystal axes (see 'Coordinate Systems and Material Orientation').

tools.name: Piezoresistive Shell (Electric Currents in Shells)
tools.description: Extension of Conductive Shell in Electric Currents in (Layered) Shells whose conductivity depends on stress or strain through the Piezoresistivity, Boundary Currents / Shell / Layered couplings (piezoresistance or elastoresistance form). In layered mode it supports General or Highly conductive layer models like Conductive Shell; without a coupling it acts as a plain conductive shell.
tools.usage: Electric Currents in Shells > Piezoresistive Shell. Java: physics("ecis").create("pzrs1", "PiezoresistiveShell", 2); set("ConstitutiveModel", "PiezoresistanceForm")

parameters.name: ConstitutiveModel
parameters.description: PiezoresistanceForm or elastoresistance form.

parameters.name: sigma0 / Pil / ml
parameters.description: Zero-stress conductivity and coupling matrices.

parameters.name: lth / coordinateSystem
parameters.description: Layer thickness and material orientation system.

tools.example: Application Library MEMS_Module/Sensors/piezoresistive_pressure_sensor: Piezoresistive Shell on the resistor boundary with a rotated coordinate system sys2.
tools.notes: Requires the MEMS Module.

tools.name: Pyroelectricity (MEMS multiphysics interface and coupling)
tools.description: Predefined interface combining Electrostatics and Heat Transfer in Solids with the Pyroelectricity coupling (pye1), which models the direct pyroelectric effect (temperature change produces polarization) and the inverse electrocaloric effect in solid dielectrics, in 3D, 2D and 2D axisymmetry. Charge Conservation (solid) represents the pyroelectric dielectric and the pyroelectric coefficients are entered on the coupling node.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics–Structure Interaction > Pyroelectricity (adds es, ht and pye1). Java: multiphysics().create("pye1", "Pyroelectricity", 3)

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Electrostatics and Heat Transfer (Solids).

parameters.name: Pyroelectric coefficients
parameters.description: Entered on the Pyroelectricity coupling node.

parameters.name: Studies
parameters.description: Stationary and Time Dependent.

tools.example: Application Library MEMS_Module/Sensors/pyroelectric_detector: chopped IR heat flux on a LiTaO3 element, transient voltage across the electrodes.
tools.notes: Requires the MEMS Module.

tools.name: Piezoelectricity and Pyroelectricity (MEMS multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface combining Solid Mechanics, Electrostatics and Heat Transfer in Solids with three couplings (Piezoelectricity, Pyroelectricity and Thermal Expansion) for devices where temperature, strain and charge interact, e.g. pyroelectric/piezoelectric sensors under thermal loading. Piezoelectric Material and Charge Conservation, Piezoelectric are the default domain nodes; available in 3D, 2D and 2D axisymmetry with the same study types as Piezoelectricity, Solid.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Electromagnetics–Structure Interaction > Piezoelectricity and Pyroelectricity

parameters.name: Piezoelectric Material (solid)
parameters.description: Elastic, coupling and permittivity data (strain-charge or stress-charge form).

parameters.name: Pyroelectricity coupling
parameters.description: Pyroelectric coefficients.

parameters.name: Thermal Expansion coupling
parameters.description: Thermal strain.

tools.example: PZT bimorph exposed to a temperature ramp: Time Dependent study of the open-circuit voltage from both pyroelectric and thermally induced piezoelectric charge.
tools.notes: Requires the MEMS Module.

tools.name: Thermoelasticity (MEMS multiphysics interface)
tools.description: Predefined interface (Solid Mechanics + Heat Transfer in Solids + Thermal Expansion coupling with thermoelastic damping heat source enabled) for thermoelastic damping (TED): tension cools and compression heats the material, and irreversible heat flow causes mechanical loss, significant for small resonators. Inertial terms are on by default and the recommended studies are Time Dependent, Thermal Perturbation, Eigenfrequency and Thermal Perturbation, Frequency Domain (a stationary step sets the baseline temperature).
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Thermal–Structure Interaction > Thermoelasticity

parameters.name: Thermoelastic damping
parameters.description: Heat source checkbox in the Thermal Expansion coupling (on).

parameters.name: Structural Transient Behavior
parameters.description: Include inertial terms (default).

parameters.name: Study
parameters.description: Thermal Perturbation, Eigenfrequency gives complex eigenfrequencies and Q = Re/(2*Im).

tools.example: Application Library MEMS_Module/Actuators/thermoelastic_damping_3d: quality factor of a silicon beam resonator from the complex eigenfrequency.
tools.notes: Temperature has a baseline and a perturbation component in frequency-domain studies.

tools.name: Squeeze-film and slide-film damping (MEMS thin-film modeling)
tools.description: MEMS modelling approach for gas films between moving microstructures and substrates using the Reynolds equation on a surface (film height h much smaller than lateral size L, inertia negligible, isothermal): squeeze-film damping for motion normal to the film, slide-film damping for tangential motion. The Thin-Film Flow interfaces (tff; Thin-Film Flow 3D/2D and Thin-Film Flow, Domain) offer full or modified Reynolds equations, slip and rarefaction models via Knudsen number and TMAC, and Perforations (e.g. Bao model); structural interfaces also provide a built-in Thin-Film Damping boundary condition.
tools.usage: Add Physics > Fluid Flow > Thin-Film Flow (Java types ThinFilmFlowShell / ThinFilmFlowEdge / ThinFilmFlowDomain); nodes Fluid-Film Properties (FluidFilmProperties), Border, Perforations; or Solid Mechanics > Thin-Film Damping

parameters.name: Equation type
parameters.description: Reynolds equation or modified Reynolds equation (ideal isothermal gas).

parameters.name: Wall/base heights and displacements
parameters.description: Height of wall above reference plane (default 10 um) and structural displacement inputs.

parameters.name: Rarefaction / slip
parameters.description: Mean free path, TMAC, slip length for high Knudsen numbers.

parameters.name: Perforations
parameters.description: Hole-flow model for perforated plates.

tools.example: Application Libraries MEMS_Module/Sensors/squeeze_film_accelerometer, squeeze_film_disc and MEMS_Module/Actuators/squeeze_film_perforated_plates (Bao perforation model).
tools.notes: Thin-Film Flow interfaces are documented in the CFD Module User's Guide and licensed with MEMS/CFD. See also Structure–Thin-Film Flow Interaction.

tools.name: Structure–Thin-Film Flow Interaction (MEMS squeeze-film coupling)
tools.description: Multiphysics coupling (stfi1) on boundaries between a thin fluid film and a solid that passes the structural velocity/displacement to the Thin-Film Flow interface and the film pressure back as a boundary load, forming the Solid–Thin-Film Damping and Shell–Thin-Film Damping interfaces. It captures squeeze- and slide-film damping and film stiffness in eigenfrequency, frequency-domain, transient and random-vibration studies of accelerometers, gyroscopes and resonators.
tools.usage: Model Wizard > Structural Mechanics > Fluid–Structure Interaction > Solid–Thin-Film Damping (adds solid, tff, stfi1). Java: multiphysics().create("stfi1", "StructureThinFilmFlowInteraction", 2)

parameters.name: Boundary selection
parameters.description: All boundaries by default; applicable fluid–solid boundaries are deduced automatically.

parameters.name: Coupled interfaces
parameters.description: Structure (Solid Mechanics/Shell) and Thin film (Thin-Film Flow).

tools.example: Application Library MEMS_Module/Sensors/squeeze_film_accelerometer: proof mass over a thin air gap; frequency response and damping ratio from Frequency Domain with the coupling active.
tools.notes: Documented in the Structural Mechanics Module User's Guide (Structure–Thin-Film Flow Interaction); available with the MEMS Module.

tools.name: Reduced-Order Modeling and Equivalent Circuits (MEMS)
tools.description: MEMS Module guidance for building reduced-order models of resonant devices: project the n-DOF system M u'' + D u' + K u = f onto a few modes within the signal bandwidth (modal coordinates), giving m-by-m modal mass, damping and stiffness that map onto lumped mechanical or electrical equivalent circuits (e.g. Butterworth–Van Dyke) for SPICE-level system simulation. COMSOL tools include Model Reduction/Modal studies, the Lumped Mechanical System interface, Parameter Estimation for fitting circuit parameters and SPICE export.
tools.usage: MEMS Module User's Guide > Creating and Analyzing MEMS Models > Reduced-Order Modeling and Equivalent Circuits; Study > Model Reduction / Eigenfrequency; Electrical Circuit > Export Spice Netlist

parameters.name: Number of modes m
parameters.description: Modes kept within the bandwidth (often one).

parameters.name: Modal mass/stiffness/damping
parameters.description: Extracted from eigenmodes and their participation.

parameters.name: Equivalent circuit
parameters.description: Motional R, L, C and static capacitance of resonators.

tools.example: Application Libraries MEMS_Module/Piezoelectric_Devices/thin_film_baw_resonator_3d_equivalent_circuit (Parameter Estimation of BVD circuit) and MEMS_Module/Sensors/capacitive_micromachined_ultrasonic_transducer_lumped_model (Lumped Mechanical System).
tools.notes: See also 'Model Reduction / Modal Reduced-Order Model' in this catalog.

tools.name: Damping and Losses in MEMS resonators (modeling guide)
tools.description: Overview of loss mechanisms that set the quality factor of MEMS devices and how to model them explicitly in COMSOL: fluid–structure interaction for viscous air damping, thin-film (squeeze/slide) damping via Thin-Film Flow or the structural Thin-Film Damping condition, thermoelastic damping with the Thermoelasticity interface, anchor losses to the substrate with Perfectly Matched Layers in the frequency domain (or spring–dampers in time domain), plus material loss factors and Rayleigh damping.
tools.usage: MEMS Module User's Guide > Structural Mechanics > Damping and Losses; combine the corresponding interfaces/couplings with Eigenfrequency or Frequency Domain studies

parameters.name: Air damping
parameters.description: FSI or Thin-Film Flow / Thin-Film Damping.

parameters.name: Thermoelastic damping
parameters.description: Thermoelasticity interface, Thermal Perturbation studies.

parameters.name: Anchor loss
parameters.description: Perfectly Matched Layer around the anchor substrate.

parameters.name: Material damping
parameters.description: Loss factor or Rayleigh damping subnodes in Solid Mechanics.

tools.example: Application Library MEMS_Module/Actuators/disc_resonator_anchor_losses: PML substrate to compute anchor-limited Q of a disc resonator.
tools.notes: Total Q follows 1/Q = sum(1/Q_i) of the individual mechanisms.
